/engines/chrome.from:
Chrome is the default engine -- no `--engine` flag is needed:

```bash
agent-browser open example.com
```

To be explicit:

```bash
agent-browser --engine chrome open example.com
```
/engines/chrome.to:
Select Chrome with the `--engine` flag:

```bash
agent-browser --engine chrome open example.com
```

Or set it as the default via environment variable or config:

```bash
AGENT_BROWSER_ENGINE=chrome agent-browser open example.com
```

```json
{
  "engine": "chrome"
}
```

An explicit engine restores the previous Chrome default and silences the fallback warning.

/files.from: `--allow-file-access` is Chromium-only. It allows `file://` pages to load and access other local files through browser APIs such as `fetch` and XHR.
/files.to:
With Chrome, `--allow-file-access` allows `file://` pages to load and access other local files through browser APIs such as `fetch` and XHR.

With Lightpanda, the default engine, `file://` pages open without the flag: agent-browser serves them from disk through a reserved host, and the page can load files from the folders the session opened (other paths return 403). `--allow-file-access` lifts that limit. A local `.pdf` relaunches the session with Chrome. See [Lightpanda local files](/engines/lightpanda#local-files).
